In mathematics, '''potential good reduction''' is a property of the [[reduction modulo a prime]] or, more generally, [[prime ideal]], of an [[algebraic variety]].

==Definitions==
"Good reduction" refers to the reduced variety having the same properties as the original, for example, an [[algebraic curve]] having the same [[genus of a curve|genus]], or a [[smooth variety]] remaining smooth. "''Potential'' good reduction" refers to the situation over a sufficiently large finite extension of the field of definition.

==Equivalent formulations==
For [[elliptic curve]]s, potential good reduction is equivalent to the [[j-invariant]] being an [[algebraic integer]].
